public_rationale: The researchers infer OpenAI employee awareness in June and report no public disclosure by September 4. That supports Marcus's concern about delayed public disclosure. It does not settle his stronger wording that OpenAI told nobody for months: the available records do not establish the first private notification or conclusively date organizational discovery.
limitations: The principal contemporaneous Reuters report could not be read with read_page.
A public-disclosure reading would be more favorable to the claim than the external-notification reading used here.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI did not disclose the German website compromise incident to anyone for months.

statement.excerpt: Once again OpenAI and told nobody for months.
statement.document_title: “I think the answer is we have to shut the labs down” - Jensen Huang

our_interpretation: The grammatical error does not obscure the allegation that OpenAI withheld disclosure of the German incident.
Read 'nobody' as no external recipient, including the affected operator, rather than only no public announcement.
Read 'months' as at least two months. In the surrounding allegation of concealment, the relevant interval begins when OpenAI knew about the incident.

The observation concerns the incident and disclosure history preceding the September 4 report identified in the post. The source supplies no exact starting date, so the target period has an unspecified start.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish that OpenAI knew about the German incident and disclosed it to no external recipient for at least two months.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish an external disclosure less than two months after OpenAI first learned of the incident.
